set.body:
Two defects in the encoding-retrieval section of introduction.Rmd, found by the vignette reviewer. Small, but they sit in the section that demonstrates the package most distinctive capability - forms whose two axes carry different named bases.

1. THE EXAMPLE NEVER CALLS THE ENGINE. introduction.Rmd:188-196 builds the cross form by hand with an ordinary matrix product of the two profile matrices. No relation(), no frame, no geometry(). Then :210 performs the contraction manually as a sum of an elementwise product. So the section that exists to show the asymmetric case being handled by the SAME algebra never routes through the algebra. A reader cannot tell whether the package supports this path or whether the vignette is illustrating a concept the package does not yet execute.

   That matters more than a normal documentation shortcut, because the unification claim IS the product. README:7-13 argues that contrast energy, RDMs, regression RSA, node effects and cross-node coupling are partial views of one evidence pairing that do not trigger separate pipelines. The unequal-axis section is where that claim is most surprising and it is demonstrated by hand arithmetic.

2. THE PROSE PROMISES A FEATURE THE CODE OMITS. introduction.Rmd:205-206 states that encoding-item and retrieval-item nuisance effects are ordinary columns in that pair-space linear model. No nuisance column appears anywhere in the example. The function that would provide it, pair_lm_query, is exported and demonstrated nowhere in either vignette - it is one of the 33 exports on bd-01KZYARD5697TRN2Q3S0E153BM.

   A reader who needs nuisance regression in an encoding-retrieval design - which is most people running one - reads that sentence, looks for the mechanism, and finds nothing.

3. THE OUTPUT IS A BARE NUMBER. The section ends on a single scalar with no units, no baseline, and no interpretation. Same failure as bd-01KZYAPHG7H569TNBPE4XV8WXN: the reader is given a value and no model of what a good one looks like.

FIX: route the example through relation() and the frame so it exercises the engine it is advertising, and either demonstrate pair_lm_query or delete the sentence promising it.
set.title: The unequal-axis example never calls the engine, and promises a feature the code omits
